HONG KONG DIPLOMA OF SECONDARY EDUCATION EXAMINATION 2026
(1) Refer to the General Instructions on Page 1 of the Question-Answer Book for Part A.
(1) The Question-Answer Book for Part B1 is inserted into this Data File.
(2) For Part B, attempt EITHER those tasks in Part B1 (Tasks 5–7) OR those in Part B2 (Tasks 8–10).
(3) You are advised to use a pen for Part B.
(4) The Data Files will NOT be collected at the end of the examination. Do NOT write your answers in the Data Files.
(5) Hand in only ONE Question-Answer Book for Part B, either B1 or B2, and tie it with the Question-Answer Book for Part A.

You are Nico Lin. You are an intern at Victoria Harbour Library. You help Ms Agnes Yip, the Assistant Librarian, in her work. You have been asked to complete some tasks.
You will listen to a recording of a staff meeting attended by Thomas Chan, the Chief Librarian, Meera Khan, the Community Engagement Officer and Agnes Yip. Take notes under the appropriate headings.
Before the recording is played, you will have five minutes to study the Question-Answer Book and the Data File to familiarise yourself with the situation and the tasks.

Complete the tasks by following the instructions in the Question-Answer Book and on the recording. You will find all the information you need in the Question-Answer Book, the Data File and on the recording. As you listen, you can make notes on page 3 of the Data File.
You now have five minutes to familiarise yourself with the Question-Answer Book and the Data File.

Listen to the recording of a staff meeting. The meeting was attended by Thomas Chan, the Chief Librarian, Meera Khan, the Community Engagement Officer and Agnes Yip, the Assistant Librarian.
Go on to the next page
This is a busy month for us, and I need you to help me out with a few different things.
First, can you update next week’s weekly schedule? We need to put it online. You can look at the email from Eddie and the Outside Speakers for Library Events table.

Secondly, we need to announce the Discover Your Library Challenge. This is a competition the previous interns developed. Can you write a post about it for our social media pages? Make sure to cover the following:
Make it sound exciting and encourage people to join. You can look at the transcript of the intern meeting, the
article and the emails from possible donors of prizes.
Thirdly, can you email Jessica Yoong to invite her to our story-reading event? In your email:
Tell her when the event is
Explain what we want her to do at the event
Tell her about the book influencer
Invite her to lunch (please choose a suitable restaurant)
You can look at my WhatsApp conversation with Meera, the
article and the Useful information about restaurants for library staff.
Listen to the recording of the staff meeting for all of these tasks.
Thanks for all your help. You’re doing a great job as our new intern.
Thank you for contacting us. Due to renovation work, we will be closed for three months, so we cannot offer a prize.

Thank you for your enquiry. We would be happy to support your Discover Your Library Challenge. Please find attached a voucher for the winner. As you will see, it’s for dinner for two. Dessert included!
We are unfortunately unable to support the Discover Your Library Challenge this year.
Go on to the next page
Okay, let’s start, I want to go for lunch.
Yeah, me too. But let’s discuss the Discover Your Library Challenge first.
Right. So, remember we said people will need to use an App to take part?
Of course. Did you try out the App?
Yeah, yesterday. It went okay. I downloaded the App – it’s called Library Search.
Okay, good so it works at least.
Yes. So, the first thing I did was I entered my full name.
Well, then basically I got the questions, and I went to different parts of the library and, you know, looked around for the answers.
Well, we only got one positive reply from the donors! So that will be the first prize.
The person with the fastest time will win the first prize.
Oh, and you have to answer all the questions correctly to win, of course.
Okay, got it. And the five runners-up? What can we give them?
We can give them those Victoria Harbour Library pens.
Okay, not very exciting but it’s fine. Can we please go for lunch now?
Which famous author has just moved to Hong Kong?
Many of our readers will be pleased to hear that Jessica Yoong, the children’s author, has recently moved to Hong Kong from Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia.
Favourite Author among Hong Kong Primary School Children

In an interview at her new home in Kennedy Town, Ms Yoong explained that she is keen to do publicity events together with influencers: ‘I really think that appearing with famous influencers can attract a wider audience.’
Ms Yoong, who is a vegetarian, is also looking forward to exploring the local food scene. She is keen to try some of our Chinese vegetarian restaurants.
Perhaps she’ll be invited to Victoria Harbour Library. She’s so popular that the waiting time there for borrowing her latest book is 5 weeks!
And speaking of Victoria Harbour Library…
Agnes Yip, the Assistant Librarian, has confirmed that the

will start later this month. They’ll be announcing details on that soon on their social media pages, but the great news is it’s not just for members – anyone can join! I’ve heard there are some great prizes.
Go on to the next page
I have a few updates and reminders for next week. You may want to tell the public about some of these.

As you know, we always test the fire alarm on Thursdays. Note that next week we’re doing it at 10 o’clock in the morning rather than the usual time of 11 o’clock. Of course, no-one is required to leave the library when the alarm goes off.
We will be fixing the wheelchair entrance on Saturday, 18 April. Wheelchair users can use the staff lift at the back of the building. I will also put up a sign at the entrance.

The Study Room on the second floor is now closed so that we can replace the floor tiles. This will mean that the Secondary School Support group meeting on Wednesday, 15 April will have a change of venue to the Study Room on the fifth floor.
We have finally hired a firm to clean all of the windows in the library. I know they have been dirty for a long time! This will be happening on Monday, 13 April between half past 9 and half past 3.
And don’t forget that on Wednesday, 29 April a team will be working on the wall next to the stairs. We will need to close the stairs on that day.
Let me know if you have any questions.
So excited about asking Jessica Yoong to the library!!
When is it? What are you planning to do exactly?
We want Jessica Yoong to read one of her stories to the primary school kids. They love those stories! Oh, and it’s on 23rd May. 11 am.
Right. That’s a Saturday. Mention that it’s a Saturday to Jessica.
I was thinking we could get the kids to dress up as one of the characters from the stories at the event.
A dress-up competition – I like it. Maybe Jessica can choose the winner?
Okay, we can ask her when we email her.
Do we need to give a prize for the best costume?
Yes! Maybe Jessica Yoong can present the winner the prize? The children would get so excited about that!
Absolutely! We can ask her to do that too.
Great. Can’t wait to meet her! Hope she says yes!
She’ll say yes if we tell her about the influencer we are going to invite! Have you chosen someone?
Yes, we’re going to ask BillReads. He’s famous!
Yeah, even I’ve heard of him!!!
